tracks.comment:
Danny Goliger has been steadily rising as one of the forefront bass & techno producers in L.A. for several years with releases on staple labels such as Dirtybird, Scuffed Recs, 3024 & Magic City alongside his residency on the renowned Dublab Radio. We are super excited to welcome him to the Faux Poly family with his stunning EP 'Say I Do.'

In Danny's own words: "Inspiration was pretty wide ranging on this EP. From UK funky, to dembow, to dubstep, post-dubstep, and garage. I've incorporated elements of these grooves and aesthetics into modern bassy club tracks."

The EP blends together two 4x4 rollers with "Say I Do" and "Weightless," alongside halftime bass led dubstep tracks "Gimme That" and "Pearls." All of these ideas were born out of modular hardware jams and delivered with Danny's distinctive ear for detail. The whole EP has already become a firm favourite within the Faux Poly family, and if you've seen any of us play this summer, then chances are you've been lucky enough to hear these on a big system already.

Buy: https://dannygoliger.bandcamp.com/album/say-i-do

DJ, Producer, Remixe�, and On-Air Mixer, SpydaT.E.K. is an all-around music chameleon. For the last few years his DJing and music has been gaining the respect and attention it rightfully deserves. tracks.comment:
Club South is growing fast and diversifying widely, inviting a generation of up-and-coming producers from the burgeoning Texas club scene to the label's very first compilation.

Having laid the foundations of the imprint with the release of several EPs, s�ngles and packs by founder Royo, followed by a series of mixes and a radio residency, the Southern label is now presenting the scene in which it gravitates.

Entitled Club South presents Pop Trunk, the release features no less than 17 tracks by 18 producers from the new wave of Texas club artists. Invited to join the party are: Amarji King, ANGIIE, Alexia Domini, Big Ace, Don Rey, goodfat, Hiram, Hustlecry, IDKRYAN, lil boi 13X, M1SSY, Nio Future, slwkng, Squincy Jones, LZRCAT, WQ, Young Brown, and of course Royo himself.

All of them are residents or regular performers at parties ranging from local clubs and bars to larger venues and sponsored events. They also host shows or have their own residencies on local community radio stations like Ice House Radio. In short, this casting highlights the existence, consistency, diversity and continuity of a truly exciting local scene.

In terms of musical styles, the release shows the plurality of club aesthetics that make up the state of Houston: juke, footwork, chopped and screwed reminiscences, Baltimore club, garage and other experimentations including Brazilian funk or the ballroom universe.

In addition to showcasing a whole scene of artists, the compilation also (above all?) has a charitable purpose: all profits will be donated to the Kid's Meals association, whose aim is to deliver free, holy meals to the neediest children in the Greater Houston area.

Club South presents Pop Trunk will be released on Bandcamp and all other platforms on June 27.

tracks.comment:
Chef’s Special (Off Menu)

Some records are made to fit neatly into a genre. This isn’t one of them.

Chef’s Special (Off Menu) is a 14-track collection of remixes, reinterpretations, and dance-floor experiments that travel through Afro house, Miami bass, Jersey club, tech house, baile funk, ghetto tech, juke, bass music, and everything in between.

The goal wasn’t to chase a trend or stay inside a lane. It was to ask a simple question: What happens when familiar songs are cooked differently?

Each track takes inspiration from a different corner of dance music culture while paying respect to the artists, cities, and communities that helped shape these sounds. Some moments are soulful. Some are high-energy. Some are built for the club at midnight. Others are meant for the ride home at 3 a.m.

This project is less of an album and more of a tasting menu. Fourteen courses. Fourteen different flavors. One kitchen.

Welcome to the Chef’s Special.

Not everything worth trying is on the menu.

The goal wasn’t to chase a trend or stay inside a lane. It was to ask a simple question: What happens when familiar songs are cooked differently?

Each track takes inspiration from a different corner of dance music culture while paying respect to the artists, cities, and communities that helped shape these sounds. Some moments are soulful. Some are high-energy. Some are built for the club at midnight. Others are meant for the ride home at 3 a.m.

This project is less of an album and more of a tasting menu. Fourteen courses. Fourteen different flavors. One kitchen.

Welcome to the Chef’s Special.

Not everything worth trying is on the menu.

tracks.comment:
HEADS KNOW has released its first-ever compilation album, US CLUB, on January 31st. Inspired by a tweet by Bok Bok that accidentally coined “US Club” — sparking rightful outrage from artists and veteran members of the club community — the platform wanted to use this project as a chance to not only educate others about club music’s true origins, but also as a chance to bring together producers from cities all over the states who’ve been helping keep club music alive today.

There’s no doubt that club music was created in Baltimore, taking direct inspiration from Ghetto House in Chicago. It spread to producers in places like Newark and Philadelphia, who added their own styles to the genre’s distinctive bounce. Now, the meaning of “club music” has morphed into almost any dancefloor-minded track made anywhere in the world. But US CLUB is an attempt to reclaim the roots of the genre while also showcasing its interpretations from various American cities.

We’re honored to feature tracks from one of Baltimore Club’s creators, DJ Technics, along with other pioneers, such as TRAXMAN and DJ Clent, who were instrumental in the evolution from ghetto house to footwork. It was also essential to have all of these tracks mastered by Nadus, a second-generation Jersey Club trailblazer who has supported HEADS KNOW since its inception.

“I handpicked all of the artists in this compilation,” HEADS KNOW founder Arielle Lana LeJarde says. “Not only did I aim to put the spotlight back on club music legends, but I also wanted to include artists who’ve made significant contributions to the scene throughout the years, plus some of my personal newer favorites.”

Other notable cuts come from DJ Problem, a member of the esteemed Brick Bandits collective, Dance Mania signee Dj Thadz, and Baltimore Club torchbearer CalvoMusic. The album also presents emerging club music mainstays bastiengoat, nextdimensional, HONEY B, Tromac, JEWELSSEA, and more.

US CLUB will be available on Bandcamp and SoundCloud. Part of its proceeds will be used to launch the HEADS KNOW Fund, which aims to distribute grants to: 1) Underground electronic music and hip-hop pioneers who are in urgent financial need of aid due to medical bills, natural disasters, or other emergencies. 2) Freelance culture journalists who need monetary assistance to complete an assignment. 3) Independent promoters that have either incurred a loss while throwing an event or will be hosting a party to raise funds for a charitable cause.

tracks.comment:
Chef’s Special (Off Menu)

Some records are made to fit neatly into a genre. This isn’t one of them.

Chef’s Special (Off Menu) is a 14-track collection of remixes, reinterpretations, and dance-floor experiments that travel through Afro house, Miami bass, Jersey club, tech house, baile funk, ghetto tech, juke, bass music, and everything in between.

The goal wasn’t to chase a trend or stay inside a lane. It was to ask a simple question: What happens when familiar songs are cooked differently?

Each track takes inspiration from a different corner of dance music culture while paying respect to the artists, cities, and communities that helped shape these sounds. Some moments are soulful. Some are high-energy. Some are built for the club at midnight. Others are meant for the ride home at 3 a.m.

This project is less of an album and more of a tasting menu. Fourteen courses. Fourteen different flavors. One kitchen.

Welcome to the Chef’s Special.

Not everything worth trying is on the menu.

tracks.path: /Users/djb.a.e/Music/DJ-Music/Music/Bouyon /santo, akalex - santo x akalex - soca funk.mp3
tracks.filename: santo, akalex - santo x akalex - soca funk.mp3
tracks.comment:
“Soca Funk” is a certified club banger, crafted for sweaty dancefloors anytime, anywhere. Co-produced by SANTO and Akalex, two DJ/producers blending their worlds into one irresistible and hybrid track, this 160 BPM heater is a full-on invitation to celebration.

The rhythm section is an explosive fusion of Cape Verdean Funaná, Caribbean Soca, and Dominican Dembow, three genres born from lands of dance, resistance, and joy. On top, a hypnotic loop of Brazilian Gaita, a nod to Baile Funk, brings an urban edge and a wildly carnival-like energy.

More than just a club banger, “Soca Funk” is a manifesto of cultural fusion, a vibrant tribute to festive traditions.
After a string of viral remixes, SANTO delivers his second official single, boldly asserting a singular sound shaped by mixed roots and a borderless musical vision.
